disclaimer: Fictional synthetic exemplars for drafting practice only. No real student data. Not legal advice.

exemplars.title: Grade 4 — Emotional Disability (anxiety), school-avoidance behaviors
exemplars.profile_summary: A fourth-grade student with an anxiety disorder whose worry about performance leads to frequent nurse visits (3–4/day), crying before tests, and incomplete work; academic skills are grade-level when calm.
strengths: Responsive to predictable routines and advance notice
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports morning stomachaches and asks for a plan that keeps the student in class rather than sending them to the nurse.
evaluation_data: Behavior rating scales completed by parent and teacher elevated for anxiety across home and school
Observation: 3–4 nurse requests/day, task avoidance during timed work, reassurance-seeking
Academic screening: grade-level reading and math when work is completed
Team determined adverse educational impact and ED eligibility; not social maladjustment

plaafp.academic: The student completes grade-level work when anxiety is managed, but turns in only 55% of assignments and has not completed a timed assessment without distress in 6 weeks. Performance is inconsistent rather than skill-based.
plaafp.functional: The student requests the nurse 3–4 times daily, cries before tests, and seeks repeated reassurance; avoids new or timed tasks. Symptoms occur across classroom, specials, and testing settings.
plaafp.impact: Anxiety-related behaviors interfere with the student's ability to access instruction and demonstrate learning, requiring a behavior support plan, counseling, and consistent adult responses that return the student to class.

baselines.measure: Daily minutes out of class/nurse visits
baselines.score: 35 minutes out of class/day; 3–4 nurse visits

goals.condition: When worried or anxious about work, tests, or changes in routine
goals.skill: use a taught coping strategy (calm breathing, self-talk, break card) and remain in class
goals.baseline: 1/10 anxious moments; 35 min/day out of class
goals.target: 8/10 anxious moments using a coping strategy with no more than 1 nurse visit/day across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: Given chunked assignments and a work-completion checklist
goals.skill: complete assigned work within the class period

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with nurse-log and work-completion data; weekly parent updates while the plan is new.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior impedes learning; positive behavior interventions, counseling, and progress monitoring are required (see behavior support plan).
supplementary_aids_services: Predictable daily schedule posted and previewed
Advance notice of tests and changes
Chunked assignments with a visible checklist
Access to a quiet reset area for 5 minutes with a pass
Check-in with a preferred adult before tests
accommodations: Extended time on tests and assignments
Testing in a small-group or familiar setting
Reduced number of items while preserving skill coverage
Option to verbalize knowledge before writing
personnel_supports: Staff training on anxiety response protocol and how to avoid reinforcing avoidance
Nurse/office protocol to return the student to class with a coping plan
exemplars.lre_statement: The student participates in general education for the full day except brief counseling and scheduled breaks. Removing the student from class in response to worry would reinforce avoidance; supports are delivered in the classroom to maintain access to grade-level instruction.
exemplars.placement: General education with related-service counseling and in-class behavior supports (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, small-group setting, and test previews. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed regression in coping routines and work completion over the prior summer; ESY is not recommended as the primary need is continued anxiety treatment. Team will reconsider with spring data. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Requests to leave class for the nurse or office, crying, and task refusal during timed or novel work.
behavior_support_plan.baseline: 3–4 nurse visits/day; 35 minutes out of class; 1/10 coping-strategy use.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Escape/avoidance of anxiety-provoking performance tasks, with reassurance-seeking maintained by adult attention.
antecedent_strategies: Preview schedule and tests the day before
Chunked work with checkpoints
Preferred adult check-in before anxiety-provoking tasks
Quiet reset pass available without leaving the classroom
replacement_behaviors_taught: Request a 2-minute break in the classroom
Ask for help using a help card
consequence_strategies: Specific praise for using a coping strategy
Brief check-in after work is attempted, not before
Nurse visits return to class as soon as coping plan is practiced
No removal of the academic task following anxiety behavior (avoid reinforcing escape)
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: If distress escalates, use calm voice, offer choice of reset location, contact counselor; if there is risk of harm, follow district crisis protocol and notify the guardian.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily tally of coping-strategy use, nurse visits, and class time retained; weekly review with the student and teacher.
staff_responsibilities: Teacher: implement antecedent supports and praise coping
Counselor: teach/practice coping strategies weekly
Office/nurse: use return-to-class protocol
Case manager: compile data for quarterly reports

source_lineage: AZ-TAS 2025 special factors and behavior guidance
PBIS Basic FBA to BSP (function-based planning)
exemplars.notes: Shows anxiety-driven avoidance with an in-class support emphasis rather than removal.

exemplars.title: Grade 2 — Emotional Disability, disruptive behavior and work refusal (FBA + BIP)
exemplars.profile_summary: A second-grade student who calls out 10–14 times per 30-minute lesson and refuses reading/writing work 2–3 times per day; an FBA identified attention and escape from difficult tasks as functions.
strengths: Responds well to humor and positive attention
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent receives daily behavior notes and wants a consistent plan that focuses on success, not punishment.
evaluation_data: FBA: ABC observations across reading, math, and recess; teacher/parent interviews
Pattern: call-outs most frequent during independent writing and when the teacher is working with other students
Rating scales elevated for attention problems and oppositional behaviors across settings
Team determined ED eligibility based on the pattern, intensity, and adverse educational impact

plaafp.academic: The student performs at grade level in math when engaged but completes only 50% of reading/writing work. Call-outs disrupt instruction 10–14 times per 30-minute block; work refusal occurs 2–3 times daily.
plaafp.functional: The student seeks adult/peer attention and escapes difficult or effortful tasks by calling out or pushing materials away. Behavior occurs across classroom and specials settings.
plaafp.impact: Disruptive and refusal behaviors interfere with the student's learning and that of classmates, requiring a function-based behavior support plan, explicit replacement-skill instruction, and structured attention.

goals.skill: raise a quiet hand and wait to be called on instead of calling out
goals.target: 0–2 call-outs per 30 minutes and appropriate hand-raising in 8/10 opportunities across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: Given a chunked assignment and a first-then routine
goals.skill: begin the first chunk within 2 minutes and complete the assigned work
goals.target: 1 or fewer refusals/day and 85% work completion across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; daily behavior report card sent home while the plan is new, then weekly.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior impedes learning and the learning of others; FBA completed and BIP included (see behavior support plan).

services.type: Special education — academic support in reading/writing

supplementary_aids_services: First-then visual and chunked work
Classroom jobs and scheduled positive attention
Break card with a 2-minute timer
Preferential seating near the teacher
Token board with a classroom reinforcement menu
accommodations: Extended time on tasks
Reduced writing demands when handwriting is not the target
Oral responses
Check for understanding before independent work begins
personnel_supports: Teacher training on planned ignoring of minor call-outs and praise ratio
Consistent language script across all staff
exemplars.lre_statement: The student remains in general education for core instruction with a behavior support plan. Pull-out time is used for explicit SEL/behavior instruction and academic support; removing the student from class as a consequence would reinforce escape and is not used except for imminent safety.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: District assessments with extended time, chunking, and frequent breaks; AASA as scheduled with permitted accommodations. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed significant regression in replacement behaviors over the prior summer with slow recoupment; ESY behavior/SEL instruction 2x/week for 30 minutes plus academic maintenance is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Calling out without raising a hand; pushing materials off the desk or refusing to begin work for more than 2 minutes after directions.
behavior_support_plan.baseline: 10–14 call-outs per 30-minute lesson; 2–3 refusals/day; 50% work completion.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Access to adult/peer attention and escape from difficult or effortful tasks.
antecedent_strategies: Pre-teach vocabulary and chunk work into 2–3 small steps
First-then visual with a preferred activity after the chunk
Scheduled 1:1 attention at the start of independent work
Movement job between subjects
Seat near a positive peer model
replacement_behaviors_taught: Raise a quiet hand and wait 3 seconds
Ask for help with a help card
Request a 2-minute break using the break card
consequence_strategies: Immediate specific praise for hand-raising and starting work
Token earned for replacement behavior; menu of reinforcers
Brief, neutral redirection for call-outs; avoid a public power struggle
Task remains available after a reset; task is not removed permanently
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: If behavior escalates to unsafe levels, use de-escalation script, clear peers, offer choice of reset locations; restraint/seclusion only if imminent danger and less restrictive options insufficient, with same-day parent notice per A.R.S. §15-105.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily frequency/refusal tallies and completion data; weekly graph review with the student; team review monthly.
staff_responsibilities: Teacher: deliver antecedent supports and data collection
SPED teacher: teach replacement skills and review data
Behavior specialist: coach fidelity and adjust plan
Case manager: communicate with family weekly

source_lineage: PBIS Basic FBA to BSP Trainer's Manual
exemplars.notes: Fully worked FBA→BIP example for mild/moderate disruptive behavior.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — Emotional Disability, aggression and crisis planning (FBA + BIP)
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student who pushes peers or throws materials 3–4 times per week, usually during transitions or when asked to stop a preferred activity; escalation pattern is predictable across a 4-stage cycle.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is worried about suspension and wants staff to use a plan that prevents escalation instead of punishment after the fact.
evaluation_data: FBA: direct observations during transitions, unstructured time, and academic demands; teacher and parent interviews
Pattern: escalation begins with pacing/arguing, escalates to verbal threats, then physical behavior when demands continue
Rating scales elevated for conduct problems and emotional dysregulation across home and school
ED eligibility determined; no cognitive or academic disability identified

plaafp.academic: The student performs near grade level when regulated but loses instructional time following incidents (average 3–4 per week), affecting progress in all subjects.
plaafp.functional: The student struggles to manage frustration during transitions and when preferred activities end; uses aggression or property destruction instead of requesting a break or accepting no.
plaafp.impact: Emotional dysregulation and aggression interfere with the student's learning, peer safety, and access to the general curriculum, requiring a function-based behavior plan, crisis protocol, and explicit coping instruction.

goals.condition: When frustrated during transitions, ending preferred activities, or academic demands
goals.skill: use a taught de-escalation strategy (signal, take a break, use calming routine) without aggression
goals.target: 8/10 events using a strategy and 0–1 physical incidents per month across 6 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: Given a 2-minute warning and a transition routine
goals.skill: transition successfully and accept 'no' or a delay without escalation
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; weekly check-in with family while incidents are above baseline.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior impedes learning and poses safety concerns; FBA and BIP completed, including a crisis plan with restraint/seclusion protocols under A.R.S. §15-105.
supplementary_aids_services: 2-minute transition warnings with a visual timer
Choice board of calming activities
Designated safe space in the classroom
Check-in/check-out with a trusted adult
Structured recess/transition routines with adult proximity
accommodations: Frequent breaks during long tasks
Extended time and chunked assignments
Alternative location for tests if needed
Opportunity to cool down before processing an incident
personnel_supports: De-escalation and crisis-script training for all staff working with the student
exemplars.lre_statement: The student remains in general education with behavior supports and a crisis plan. Brief pull-out sessions teach regulation skills; the team avoids exclusionary responses to behavior because they reinforce escape and increase future incidents. Removal occurs only for imminent safety, with return to class as soon as possible.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services and related-service counseling (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, frequent breaks, small-group setting, and crisis supports available. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student has shown severe regression in regulation skills over summer with slow recoupment and is at a critical transition point to middle school; ESY behavior/SEL programming 3x/week for 30 minutes with a transition component is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Physical aggression (pushing, hitting), throwing materials, and verbal threats during transitions or when preferred activities end.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Escape/avoidance of non-preferred demands and transitions; access to preferred activity/control.
antecedent_strategies: 2-minute warnings and visual timers before transitions
First-then schedule with preferred activity earned
Offer acceptable choices to increase control
Adult proximity during known trigger times (hallway, recess end)
Pre-teach and rehearse transition routine
replacement_behaviors_taught: Use the 'break' signal and take a 2-minute regulated break
Use a calming routine (breathing, wall push, drink of water)
Ask for help or negotiate a delay appropriately
Use an 'I feel' statement instead of threats
consequence_strategies: Reinforce replacement behavior immediately with praise and access to the earned activity
Neutral, brief redirection; avoid power struggles
After an incident, complete a processing sheet once calm (restorative conversation)
Consistent consequences for aggression per district code, paired with teaching, not exclusion alone
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: Stages: (1) pacing/arguing — offer break and reduce demands; (2) verbal threats — clear space, use calm short phrases, call for crisis-trained staff; (3) physical behavior — ensure peer safety, follow district crisis protocol; restraint/seclusion only if imminent danger and less restrictive interventions insufficient, with continuous monitoring, immediate end when danger passes, and same-day parent notice (within 24 hours if needed) plus written documentation per A.R.S. §15-105. Any repeated use triggers a team review including whether the FBA/BIP needs revision.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily incident log (frequency, duration, antecedents, staff response), transition checklist, weekly graph review with the student and team.
staff_responsibilities: Teacher: transitions, warnings, data
Crisis-trained staff: de-escalation and safety
Counselor: weekly skill practice and processing
Behavior specialist: fidelity checks and plan revisions
Case manager: parent communication and documentation

source_lineage: PBIS Basic FBA to BSP Trainer's Manual

exemplars.title: Grade 3 — OHI/ADHD, inattention and off-task behavior (BIP)
exemplars.profile_summary: A third-grade student with ADHD who is on task for an average of 11 minutes of a 30-minute independent work block, loses materials, and blurts answers; academic skills are grade level when work is completed.
strengths: Thrives with movement and hands-on tasks
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent asks that the teacher use movement and frequent feedback rather than repeated reprimands.
evaluation_data: Medical diagnosis of ADHD documented by a physician
Teacher/parent rating scales elevated for inattention and hyperactivity across settings
Observation: on task 11 of 30 minutes during independent work; blurting 8–10 times per lesson
OHI eligibility determined; adverse educational impact documented

plaafp.academic: The student performs at grade level in reading and math when work is completed, but completes only 60% of independent work. Off-task behavior averages 19 minutes per 30-minute block; assignment materials are lost 2–3 times per week.
plaafp.functional: Sustained attention, impulse control, and organization are the primary needs. The student benefits from movement, chunked tasks, timers, and immediate feedback.
plaafp.impact: ADHD-related inattention and impulsivity interfere with independent work production and classroom participation, requiring behavior supports, SDI in organization/attention strategies, and accommodations.

goals.condition: During a 30-minute independent work block with chunked tasks, a timer, and scheduled breaks
goals.skill: remain on task and complete chunks
goals.target: 25 of 30 minutes on task and 90% completion across 4 of 5 days for 4 consecutive weeks
goals.measurement: Interval observation twice weekly; daily assignment log
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.skill: use a waiting strategy (write it down, hold-up signal) instead of blurting
goals.target: 0–2 blurts per lesson across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; weekly progress note home while the plan is new.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior impedes learning; a function-based behavior support plan is included, emphasizing antecedent supports and self-monitoring rather than consequences.
supplementary_aids_services: Chunked assignments with a visual timer
Movement breaks every 10–12 minutes
Fidget/movement tool that does not distract peers
Preferential seating near instruction
Self-monitoring checklist and daily goal card
accommodations: Extended time on assignments and assessments
Frequent breaks during testing
Reduced copying; printed notes
Directions repeated/checked for understanding
Testing in a low-distraction setting
personnel_supports: Teacher training on ADHD-friendly instruction and positive redirection
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is educated in general education for the full day with in-class behavior supports and pull-out SDI for attention/organization skills. Pull-out is needed to teach self-monitoring skills with immediate feedback; behavior supports are delivered in the classroom so the student is not removed as a consequence.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, frequent breaks, low-distraction setting, and chunking. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student regressed over the prior summer in reading fluency and work habits with slow recoupment; ESY academic and attention-strategy sessions 2x/week for 30 minutes are recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Off-task behavior (looking away, playing with objects, leaving seat) during independent work; blurting answers without raising a hand.
behavior_support_plan.baseline: 11 of 30 minutes on task; 8–10 blurts per lesson; 60% work completion.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Escape from sustained effort/attention demands; stimulation needs; occasional attention from peers.
antecedent_strategies: Chunk work with a visual timer (5–7 minute chunks)
Movement break between chunks
Preferential seating and eye contact before directions
Choice of task order
Fidget tool and standing option
replacement_behaviors_taught: Self-monitoring: check the timer and mark the checklist
Write down the idea instead of blurting; use a hand signal for urgent questions
Request a movement break with a break card
consequence_strategies: Specific praise and points for on-task intervals and hand-raising
Neutral redirection back to the chunk; avoid long verbal reprimands
If work is incomplete, use a scheduled completion time rather than removing recess as a first response
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: No safety concerns; if escalation occurs, provide a movement break and check-in with a trusted adult.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily work log, twice-weekly interval observations, and blurting counts; weekly review with the student; monthly team review.
staff_responsibilities: Teacher: timers, chunks, data
SPED teacher: teach self-monitoring and review data
Family: daily goal-card review and return

source_lineage: AZ-TAS 2025 behavior special factor and OHI framing
PBIS Basic FBA to BSP antecedent strategies
exemplars.notes: Shows ADHD-focused antecedent supports rather than punishment; includes a medical diagnosis as part of OHI evaluation data.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — OHI/ADHD, executive function and organization
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student with ADHD who understands grade-level content but loses homework, forgets materials, and rushes work, resulting in 55% assignment completion despite accurate in-class performance.
strengths: Strong verbal skills and class participation
Performs well on work completed in class
Motivated by checklists and earning responsibility
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent says mornings and homework are a daily battle over forgotten materials and lost assignments.
evaluation_data: Medical diagnosis of ADHD
Teacher/parent rating scales elevated for inattention and organizational problems
Gradebook audit: 55% assignment completion with high accuracy on submitted work
OHI eligibility determined; needs are executive-function related

plaafp.academic: Submitted work is accurate and at grade level, but only 55% is turned in; the student often completes homework and forgets to submit it. Test grades are lower than daily work due to rushed preparation.
plaafp.functional: The student lacks a consistent system for tracking assignments, managing materials, and planning multi-day tasks; benefits from checklists, digital reminders, and adult check-ins.
plaafp.impact: ADHD-related executive-function needs interfere with demonstrating learning across all subjects and require explicit organization instruction, accommodations, and a functional goal.

goals.condition: Given a planner, digital assignment list, and daily check-ins
goals.skill: record, organize, and submit assignments on time
goals.target: 90% completion and 5/5 prepared days across 4 consecutive weeks

goals.condition: Given a project checklist with interim due dates
goals.skill: plan and complete checkpoints on time

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with gradebook and checkpoint data; weekly planner check sent home.

services.type: Special education — academic support (test prep/study skills)

supplementary_aids_services: Shared digital assignment calendar
Paper planner with teacher initials
Duplicate set of textbooks at home
Checklists for multi-step work
Morning check-in with case manager
accommodations: Extended time on assignments and tests
Reduced penalty for late work while organization goals are being taught per district policy
Digital submission option
Testing in a low-distraction setting
personnel_supports: Coordination with front office for forgotten materials without shaming
exemplars.lre_statement: The student participates in general education for core instruction; pull-out sessions teach organization and study skills that cannot be delivered with whole-class pacing. Supports are embedded in general education classes to build independence.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, chunking, and low-distraction setting. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed significant regression in organizational routines over the summer with slow recoupment; ESY study-skills sessions 2x/week for 30 minutes with a reading maintenance component are recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
source_lineage: Missouri DESE PLAAFP and SMART Goal rubrics
exemplars.notes: Contrast with SLD executive-function exemplar: here the category is OHI and academic SDI focuses on study skills/test prep.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — Emotional Disability (depression/withdrawal), participation and safety monitoring
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student with depression who puts their head down or refuses to participate on 4 of 5 days, has withdrawn from peer activities, and is academically capable when engaged; safety monitoring is part of the plan.
strengths: Gentle with animals and younger siblings
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports the student comes home exhausted and has stopped seeing friends; requests school and therapy to work together.
evaluation_data: Parent and teacher rating scales elevated for depressive symptoms and withdrawal
Observation: head down/refusal 4 of 5 days; no disruptive behavior
Outside mental-health provider confirms diagnosis; parent consented to coordination
Team determined ED eligibility and adverse educational impact

plaafp.academic: The student is capable of grade-level work but completes approximately 40% of assignments, participates in fewer than 1 of 5 class activities, and has withdrawn from all extracurricular activities.
plaafp.functional: Low mood, fatigue, and social withdrawal limit participation and connection; the student needs gentle engagement, predictable check-ins, and safety monitoring.
plaafp.impact: Depressive symptoms and withdrawal interfere with access to grade-level instruction and peer relationships, requiring counseling, participation supports, and a monitored safety plan.

goals.condition: Given preferred activity options and a caring adult check-in
goals.skill: participate in class activities and complete assigned work
goals.target: 3 of 5 activities and 80% work completion across 3 consecutive weeks
goals.measurement: Daily participation tally and assignment log
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: Given structured small-group and partner activities
goals.skill: initiate or respond to two peer interactions per day
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; weekly check-in with parent while risk monitoring is active.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Behavior (withdrawal) impedes learning; counseling and a monitored support plan are required. Safety monitoring follows district risk protocol.

services.provider: School counselor (coordinating with outside therapist with consent)

supplementary_aids_services: Morning check-in with a preferred adult
Small-group and partner structures for participation
Choice of activity and reduced social pressure
Access to art/writing outlets and quiet space
accommodations: Extended time and reduced workload during low periods (preserving essential skills)
Option to complete work in a quiet area or with a trusted peer
Oral responses
Breaks without penalty
personnel_supports: Staff training on depression signs and referral protocol
Coordination of care with outside mental-health provider (with parent consent)
exemplars.lre_statement: The student stays in general education with counseling, check-in/check-out, and participation supports. Pull-out academic support is used gently to avoid additional isolation; participation in general education activities, including preferred electives, is prioritized.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services and related-service counseling (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, quiet setting, breaks, and alternate scheduling if needed. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student has a pattern of significant regression in participation and academic skills during summer; ESY structure is recommended for social/emotional connection and academic maintenance, 2x/week for 45 minutes. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.

behavior_support_plan.target_behavior_operational: Putting head down, not responding to instruction, not participating in activities, and withdrawing from peers.
behavior_support_plan.baseline: 4/5 days with head down/refusal; 1 of 5 activities; 40% work completion; 0–1 peer interactions/day.
behavior_support_plan.hypothesized_function: Low mood and fatigue reduce available energy; avoidance of social/performance demands also functions to reduce distress.
antecedent_strategies: Warm morning greeting and private check-in
Offer choice of activity and reduced social pressure
Break tasks into very small steps with immediate success
Invite (do not force) participation; provide quiet alternative with the same content
replacement_behaviors_taught: Use a feelings check-in card to communicate mood
Ask for a break or quiet space appropriately
Choose one participation goal per class to work on
Initiate one structured peer interaction using a script
consequence_strategies: Immediate positive acknowledgment for any participation
Restorative, non-punitive follow-up if work is not completed
Reinforce peer interactions naturally with activity access
behavior_support_plan.crisis_plan: Staff monitor for risk indicators daily. If the student expresses self-harm or is unsafe, follow the district crisis protocol: stay with the student, notify the counselor/administrator immediately, contact the parent, and make a safety plan. Outside provider coordination occurs with written parent consent. If the student leaves class, follow the individualized safe-return plan rather than pursuit that escalates distress.
behavior_support_plan.progress_monitoring: Daily participation and interaction tallies, weekly counselor data review, weekly parent communication, and monthly team check.
staff_responsibilities: Teacher: welcoming check-in, participation supports, data
Counselor: weekly sessions, risk monitoring, family/outside-provider coordination
Case manager: monitor data and convene the team if no progress
All staff: know the crisis protocol

source_lineage: PBIS Basic FBA to BSP (function-based supports)
exemplars.notes: Shows a non-disruptive behavioral profile with safety monitoring; underscores why the tool must treat behavior as broader than disruption.
